title: Introduction to Redis
subtitle: What Redis is, its use cases, and architecture

content.text: Redis (Remote Dictionary Server) is an in-memory key-value store. Because it stores data in RAM, it is extremely fast — capable of millions of operations per second.

content.definition: Data is stored in RAM rather than on disk, making access nanoseconds instead of milliseconds.

content.code:
# Install Redis (macOS)
brew install redis
brew services start redis

# Connect
redis-cli
127.0.0.1:6379> PING
PONG

content.text: Redis is single-threaded for command execution, which eliminates race conditions without locks.

questions.question: Where does Redis primarily store data?
questions.explanation: Redis stores data in RAM for maximum speed.

faq.a: Yes. Redis supports RDB snapshots and AOF (Append-Only File) persistence to survive restarts.
